title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that isolates downstream verifier/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic stress corpus (Ntasks = 1000) and a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), we compared a baseline single‑shot LLM generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (one permitted repair call and a canary stage). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and the preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) froze the design before any hosted‑model calls. Observed paired outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). A preregistered descriptive paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]; because the paired design used a shared initial candidate, any paired benefit can only arise from deterministic validation and permitted repairs. We report the exact McNemar result as the confirmatory outcome, explicitly label a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory (not prespecified), and discuss the interpretive limits imposed by very high baseline validity and sparse discordant counts.

sections.introduction:
Automating natural‑language intent → device configuration translation promises operational efficiency for network operations, but it also creates safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and unintended modification of protected fields can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior work documents that large language models (LLMs) are prompt‑sensitive and prone to structured‑output failures (hallucinations and syntactic/semantic errors) that materially affect executable artifacts [1],[2]. Architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures have been proposed to mitigate these risks, but empirical evidence quantifying how much downstream validation and constrained repair alone contribute—distinct from prompt engineering or constrained decoding—is limited [3],[4],[5].

This study answers a tightly scoped question under a preregistered paired design: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate), to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus at most one permitted repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? By holding the initial sample constant across arms, the design isolates downstream validator/repair effects and prevents attributing any paired difference to independent first‑pass generation variance, prompt engineering, or constrained decoding that were not executed.
sections.related_work:
Empirical surveys and controlled studies show that LLMs commonly produce hallucinations, exhibit prompt sensitivity, and make structured‑output mistakes that reduce correctness in code and configuration tasks; mitigation approaches include schema constraints, constrained decoding, and verifier‑assisted repair [1],[2],[3]. Several recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system works propose verifier‑assisted architectures and governance mechanisms (proof‑carrying actions, protocol‑mediated execution) to improve operational trustworthiness, usually demonstrated in prototypes or synthetic evaluations rather than large production trials [4],[5],[6].

Our study complements this literature by preregistering a paired estimand that isolates the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation and a single limited repair when the initial candidate is shared. This isolates the contribution of verifier+repair layers from any changes that would arise from independent first‑pass generation or alternative prompting arms, which remain important but separate interventions for future controlled evaluation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design fidelity. The experiment was preregistered as cand‑003‑stud‑001 and frozen prior to any hosted‑model calls (preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Key preregistered choices: paired binary confirmatory design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks drawn from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries included a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) used only as a descriptive summary.

Execution and validators. The declared model/provider recorded in the archived model configuration is gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The runtime model configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The orchestration adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator version 5.0). The validator deterministically enforces manifest‑declared workflow policies (required sequence ordering, allowed_touched_fields, protected interfaces) via a digital‑twin emulator and returns a binary safe‑deploy outcome together with structured validator traces archived per episode.

Sampling, pairing, and missingness. Tasks were selected deterministically by the preregistered ordinal rule to produce exactly 1000 pairs. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes; only deterministic validation and the permitted single repair call could produce paired outcome differences. The preregistration prespecified a 'complete_pair_primary' missingness treatment; execution followed that plan with no failed episodes recorded.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and artifacts. The run completed the preregistered episodes: planned_episode_count = 2000; completed_episode_count = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000. Provider call audit records hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005 (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 1000; repair = 5). No failed hosted model calls were recorded and contamination/exclusion checks found no prompt‑leakage flags.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test. The preregistered 2×2 paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; because this was the preregistered primary analysis, H1 is not supported at two‑sided α = 0.05.

Descriptive bootstrap summary and exploratory directional test. The preregistered descriptive paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01] (artifact: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The bootstrap summary was preregistered as descriptive only. We also computed an exploratory/post‑hoc one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) that yields p = 0.03125; this one‑sided test was not prespecified and is explicitly reported as exploratory. Why the bootstrap CI can exclude zero despite a nonsignificant two‑sided McNemar: bootstrap percentile intervals on proportions or paired differences are sensitive when discordant counts are extremely sparse (here n10 + n01 = 5), so resampling variability and the percentile procedure can produce percentile bounds that do not include zero even when the exact conditional McNemar two‑sided test crosses the α = 0.05 threshold. The bootstrap details—including contingency table contents and bootstrap_seed = 1729—are archived with the run for inspection.

Repair mechanics and representative traces. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair stage_count = 5). Representative episode artifacts (execution/scoring/task‑00000*.json) show repairs invoked for ordering or protected‑field touches and accepted after revalidation. All raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces (where present), and validator traces are archived and referenced in the deterministic reconciliation artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory hierarchy, preregistration fidelity, and interpretive caution. The preregistered confirmatory analysis is the exact two‑sided McNemar test; that test produced p = 0.0625 and therefore does not meet the preregistered α = 0.05 threshold. The paired bootstrap CI and the post‑hoc one‑sided McNemar are reported for descriptive and exploratory context only and do not overturn the preregistered confirmatory null. We emphasize this hierarchy because the preregistered design deliberately isolated downstream effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics: paired gains can only stem from deterministic validation and permitted repairs, not from first‑pass generation changes.

Why the observed regime limits detectability. The preregistered power plan targeted an effect size (absolute increase ≈ 0.15) under an assumed baseline ≈ 0.60. The observed baseline success rate was 0.995, far above that assumption; near‑unity baseline rates produce very few discordant pairs and therefore substantially reduce sensitivity of the planned exact paired test to detect small absolute improvements. This power‑assumption mismatch is artifact‑grounded in the preregistration and execution manifests and explains the apparent tension between the nonsignificant two‑sided McNemar and a bootstrap CI that excludes zero.

Mechanistic implications and limitations. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics only deterministic validator decisions and the single allowed repair could change paired outcomes. The five observed repairs show that a validator with sufficient rule coverage can correct certain sequence/order violations; however, the small repair count constrains inference about repair efficacy across diverse failure modes. External validity is limited by the single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), the synthetic task corpus, and the deterministic validator rule set. Construct validity depends on validator coverage: omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Follow‑ups should vary generator semantics (independent initial generations), expand repair budgets, broaden validator rule sets and topology heterogeneity, and include multiple model families, each with preregistered power calculations appropriate to anticipated baseline failure prevalence.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study (Npairs = 1000) that held the initial sampled candidate constant across arms, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls invoiced by the adapter were 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). These artifact‑grounded results indicate that downstream verifier/repair safeguards can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Archival artifacts include the preregistration, raw responses, validator traces, contingency tables, and bootstrap parameters (seed = 1729) to support reproducibility and to inform preregistered follow‑ups that broaden model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

Preregistration: cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls). Immutable initial master prompt reference archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). After the autonomy lock the research run performed literature review, preregistration finalization, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
